title: Chinese Hackers Quietly Used Low-Severity ESXi Logging Flaw as Zero-Day
content_md: The US cybersecurity agency CISA on Wednesday warned that hackers have been exploiting another VMware ESXi vulnerability in attacks. Tracked as CVE-2026-41709, the exploited flaw is described as a low-severity insufficient logging issue. It allows attackers logged in as administrators to perform certain operations without being logged. The security defect was disclosed on July 29 alongside three critical and one high-severity bug in VMware vCenter, ESXi, Workstation, and Fusion. VMware ESXi-9.1.0.0-25370933, ESXi-9.0.2.0100-25595025, and ESXi80U3j-25429389 and newer releases contain the relevant patches. CISA added CVE-2026-41709 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities ( KEV ) catalog, urging federal agencies to patch it within the next two weeks. CISA did not provide details on the observed exploitation, but CrowdStrike reported on Wednesday that the China-nexus threat actor Warp Panda had exploited CVE-2026-41709 as a zero-day in intrusions at US organizations, including law firms. According to CrowdStrike, Warp Panda typically gains initial access through internet-facing edge devices and pivots to VMware vCenter, where it deployed malware such as BrickStorm, TetanusStorm, SharpStorm, DualGauge and GuestConduit in intrusions throughout 2025.
